dict.string: Compare selected Finder files locally, ask the configured AI only when needed, and open the report in CompareFilesViewer. Requires macOS 26+, the viewer app, and a configured Use Model action. AI input includes file names, paths, metadata, text excerpts and comparison evidence.

Shortcuts generated by Shortcuts Playground. May contain mistakes. Always check the shortcut's actions first.
This shortcut was created via the following user prompt:
> Adapt the supplied Compare Files shortcut for open-source use, including portable installation paths and documented scripts.

set -u
# ============================================================ # Compare Files — Local Analyzer # # Output ALWAYS JSON: # # status = ERROR # # status = LOCAL_RESULT # # status = AI_REQUIRED # # ============================================================
# ------------------------------------------------------------ # JSON helpers # ------------------------------------------------------------
json_string() { /usr/bin/printf '%s' "${1-}" | /usr/bin/perl \ -MJSON::PP \ -MEncode \ -0777 \ -e ' use strict; use warnings;
binmode STDIN, ":raw"; binmode STDOUT, ":raw";
local $/; my $raw = <STDIN>; $raw = "" unless defined $raw;
my $text;
eval { $text = Encode::decode( "UTF-8", $raw, Encode::FB_CROAK ); };
if ($@) { $text = Encode::decode( "UTF-8", $raw, Encode::FB_DEFAULT ); }
print JSON::PP ->new ->utf8 ->allow_nonref ->encode($text); ' }
json_nullable_string() { local value="${1-}"
if [[ -n "$value" && "$value" != "(null)" ]]; then json_string "$value" else print -rn -- "null" fi }
json_number_or_null() { local value="${1-}"
if [[ "$value" == <-> ]]; then print -rn -- "$value" else print -rn -- "null" fi }
emit_simple_error() { local message="${1-Unknown error}"
print -rn -- '{"schema_version":1,"status":"ERROR","error":' json_string "$message" print -r -- '}' }
# ------------------------------------------------------------ # Input validation # ------------------------------------------------------------
if (( $# < 2 )); then emit_simple_error \ "Please select at least 2 files in Finder before running Compare Files." exit 0 fi
# ------------------------------------------------------------ # Temporary workspace # ------------------------------------------------------------
TMPBASE="${TMPDIR:-/tmp/}" [[ "$TMPBASE" == */ ]] || TMPBASE="${TMPBASE}/"
WORKDIR_CF="$( /usr/bin/mktemp \ -d \ "${TMPBASE}CompareFiles.XXXXXX" )" || { emit_simple_error \ "Unable to create the Compare Files temporary directory." exit 0 }
cleanup() { /bin/rm -rf "$WORKDIR_CF" 2>/dev/null || true }
trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM HUP
# ------------------------------------------------------------ # Arrays # ------------------------------------------------------------
integer idx=0
typeset -a paths typeset -a names typeset -a exts typeset -a sizes typeset -a created typeset -a modified typeset -a hashes
typeset -a families typeset -a media_info
typeset -a text_sigs typeset -a text_files typeset -a diff_text_files typeset -a text_bytes
typeset -a image_indices
typeset -a image_pair_a typeset -a image_pair_b typeset -a image_pair_scores
integer image_pair_limit_reached=0 integer text_pair_limit_reached=0
# ------------------------------------------------------------ # Helpers # ------------------------------------------------------------
lower() { print -r -- "$1" | /usr/bin/tr \ '[:upper:]' \ '[:lower:]' }
normalize_family() { local n="$1"
n="${n%.*}"
print -r -- "$n" | /usr/bin/perl \ -CSDA \ -pe ' for (1..4) {
s/\s*\(\d+\)\s*$//;
s/[\s._-]+(?: copy| duplicate| backup| bak| new| latest| final(?:[-_ ]*final)?\d*| rev(?:ision)?[-_ ]*\d+| ver(?:sion)?[-_ ]*\d+| v\d+(?:\.\d+)*| 副本| 复制| 备份| 最新版| 最终版| 定稿| 修订版\d* )\s*$//ix;
s/[\s._-]+20\d{2}[-.]?\d{1,2}[-.]?\d{1,2}\s*$//; }
s/[\s._-]+$//; ' | /usr/bin/tr \ '[:upper:]' \ '[:lower:]' }
extract_text() { local f="$1" local ext="$2" local out="$3"
: > "$out"
case "$ext" in
txt|md|markdown|csv|tsv|json|xml|html|htm|log)
/bin/cat \ "$f" \ 2>/dev/null \ > "$out" \ || true ;;
rtf|rtfd|doc|docx|odt|pages)
if [[ -x /usr/bin/textutil ]]; then
/usr/bin/textutil \ -convert txt \ -stdout \ "$f" \ 2>/dev/null \ > "$out" \ || true
fi ;;
pdf)
/usr/bin/mdls \ -raw \ -name kMDItemTextContent \ "$f" \ 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/sed \ '/^(null)$/d' \ > "$out" \ || true ;;
pptx|ppsx)
if [[ -x /usr/bin/unzip ]]; then
/usr/bin/unzip \ -p \ "$f" \ 'ppt/slides/slide*.xml' \ 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/perl \ -CSDA \ -pe ' s#</a:p>#\n#g; s#<[^>]+># #g; s/&/&/g; s/</</g; s/>/>/g; s/"/"/g; s/'/'"'"'/g; s/[ \t\r]+/ /g; ' \ > "$out" \ || true
fi ;;
xlsx|xlsm)
if [[ -x /usr/bin/unzip ]]; then
/usr/bin/unzip \ -p \ "$f" \ 'xl/sharedStrings.xml' \ 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/perl \ -CSDA \ -pe ' s#</t>#\n#g; s#<[^>]+># #g; s/&/&/g; s/</</g; s/>/>/g; s/"/"/g; s/'/'"'"'/g; s/[ \t\r]+/ /g; ' \ > "$out" \ || true
fi ;;
*)
/usr/bin/mdls \ -raw \ -name kMDItemTextContent \ "$f" \ 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/sed \ '/^(null)$/d' \ > "$out" \ || true ;; esac }
prepare_diff_text() { local input="$1" local output="$2"
if [[ ! -s "$input" ]]; then : > "$output" return fi
/usr/bin/perl \ -CSDA \ -pe ' s/\r$//; s/[ \t]+$//; ' \ "$input" \ > "$output" \ 2>/dev/null \ || true }
truncate_diff_line() { /usr/bin/printf '%s' "${1-}" | /usr/bin/perl \ -MEncode \ -0777 \ -e ' use strict; use warnings;
binmode STDIN, ":raw"; binmode STDOUT, ":raw";
local $/; my $raw = <STDIN>; $raw = "" unless defined $raw;
my $text = Encode::decode( "UTF-8", $raw, Encode::FB_DEFAULT );
$text =~ s/[ \t]+/ /g;
if (length($text) > 400) { $text = substr($text, 0, 400) . "…"; }
print Encode::encode("UTF-8", $text); ' }
emit_sample_lines_json() { local file="$1" integer max_lines="${2:-6}" integer n=0 integer first=1 local line="" local shortened=""
print -rn -- '['
while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n "$line" ]]; do
(( ++n ))
if (( n > max_lines )); then break fi
shortened="$( truncate_diff_line "$line" )"
if (( ! first )); then print -rn -- ',' fi
first=0
json_string "$shortened"
done < "$file"
print -rn -- ']' }
# ------------------------------------------------------------ # Read selected files # ------------------------------------------------------------
for f in "$@"; do
(( ++idx ))
paths[$idx]="$f" names[$idx]="${f:t}"
if [[ ! -e "$f" ]]; then
emit_simple_error \ "Unable to read file: ${names[$idx]}. The file does not exist or has been moved."
exit 0 fi
if [[ ! -f "$f" ]]; then
emit_simple_error \ "Folder comparison is not currently supported: ${names[$idx]}."
exit 0 fi
# -------------------------------------------------------- # Basic metadata # --------------------------------------------------------
local_ext="${f:e}"
exts[$idx]="$( lower "$local_ext" )"
sizes[$idx]="$( /usr/bin/stat \ -f '%z' \ "$f" \ 2>/dev/null \ || true )"
created[$idx]="$( /usr/bin/mdls \ -raw \ -name kMDItemFSCreationDate \ "$f" \ 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/sed \ -E \ ' /^(null)$/d s/ \+0000$// ' \ || true )"
modified[$idx]="$( /usr/bin/stat \ -f '%Sm' \ -t '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %z' \ "$f" \ 2>/dev/null \ || true )"
hashes[$idx]="$( /usr/bin/shasum \ -a 256 \ "$f" \ 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/awk \ '{print $1}' )"
if [[ -z "${hashes[$idx]}" ]]; then
emit_simple_error \ "Unable to calculate SHA-256 for file: ${names[$idx]}."
exit 0 fi
families[$idx]="$( normalize_family \ "${names[$idx]}" )"
# -------------------------------------------------------- # Extract text # --------------------------------------------------------
tf="$WORKDIR_CF/text-$idx.txt"
extract_text \ "$f" \ "${exts[$idx]}" \ "$tf"
text_files[$idx]="$tf"
# -------------------------------------------------------- # Prepare normalized text for line diff # --------------------------------------------------------
dtf="$WORKDIR_CF/diff-text-$idx.txt"
prepare_diff_text \ "$tf" \ "$dtf"
diff_text_files[$idx]="$dtf"
if [[ -s "$tf" ]]; then
text_bytes[$idx]="$( /usr/bin/stat \ -f '%z' \ "$tf" \ 2>/dev/null \ || print -r -- "0" )"
# Complete extracted text signature. # # Whitespace is normalized, but CASE IS PRESERVED. # This means case changes are also detected. text_sigs[$idx]="$( /usr/bin/tr \ -s \ '[:space:]' \ ' ' \ < "$tf" | /usr/bin/shasum \ -a 256 | /usr/bin/awk \ '{print $1}' )"
else
text_bytes[$idx]="0" text_sigs[$idx]=""
fi
# -------------------------------------------------------- # Media metadata # --------------------------------------------------------
case "${exts[$idx]}" in
jpg|jpeg|png|heic|heif|tif|tiff|gif|bmp|webp)
image_indices+=("$idx")
w="$( /usr/bin/sips \ -g pixelWidth \ "$f" \ 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/awk \ '/pixelWidth:/{print $2}' )"
h="$( /usr/bin/sips \ -g pixelHeight \ "$f" \ 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/awk \ '/pixelHeight:/{print $2}' )"
fmt="$( /usr/bin/sips \ -g format \ "$f" \ 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/awk \ '/format:/{print $2}' )"
media_info[$idx]="Image ${w:-?}×${h:-?}, format ${fmt:-${exts[$idx]}}" ;;
*)
pages="$( /usr/bin/mdls \ -raw \ -name kMDItemNumberOfPages \ "$f" \ 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/sed \ '/^(null)$/d' )"
ctype="$( /usr/bin/mdls \ -raw \ -name kMDItemContentType \ "$f" \ 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/sed \ '/^(null)$/d' )"
if [[ -n "$pages" ]]; then
media_info[$idx]="${ctype:-${exts[$idx]}}, pages ${pages}"
else
media_info[$idx]="${ctype:-${exts[$idx]}}"
fi ;; esac
done
# ------------------------------------------------------------ # Exact duplicate fast path # ------------------------------------------------------------
integer all_same=1
for (( i=2; i<=idx; i++ )); do
if [[ "${hashes[$i]}" != "${hashes[1]}" ]]; then
all_same=0 break
fi
done
# ------------------------------------------------------------ # Image similarity evidence # ------------------------------------------------------------
if (( ! all_same && ${#image_indices[@]} >= 2 )); then
integer pair_count=0
for (( a=1; a<=${#image_indices[@]}; a++ )); do
i=${image_indices[$a]}
for (( b=a+1; b<=${#image_indices[@]}; b++ )); do
j=${image_indices[$b]}
(( ++pair_count ))
if (( pair_count > 30 )); then
image_pair_limit_reached=1 break 2
fi
bmp1="$WORKDIR_CF/image-$i.bmp" bmp2="$WORKDIR_CF/image-$j.bmp"
if [[ ! -f "$bmp1" ]]; then
/usr/bin/sips \ -z 64 64 \ -s format bmp \ "${paths[$i]}" \ --out "$bmp1" \ >/dev/null 2>&1 \ || true
fi
if [[ ! -f "$bmp2" ]]; then
/usr/bin/sips \ -z 64 64 \ -s format bmp \ "${paths[$j]}" \ --out "$bmp2" \ >/dev/null 2>&1 \ || true
fi
score=""
if [[ -s "$bmp1" && -s "$bmp2" ]]; then
od1="$WORKDIR_CF/od-$i.txt" od2="$WORKDIR_CF/od-$j.txt"
/usr/bin/tail \ -c +55 \ "$bmp1" | /usr/bin/od \ -An \ -tu1 \ -v | /usr/bin/tr \ -s \ ' ' \ '\n' | /usr/bin/sed \ '/^$/d' \ > "$od1"
/usr/bin/tail \ -c +55 \ "$bmp2" | /usr/bin/od \ -An \ -tu1 \ -v | /usr/bin/tr \ -s \ ' ' \ '\n' | /usr/bin/sed \ '/^$/d' \ > "$od2"
score="$( /usr/bin/paste \ "$od1" \ "$od2" | /usr/bin/awk ' NF == 2 {
d = $1 - $2
if (d < 0) d = -d
total += d count++ }
END {
if (count > 0) printf "%.5f", total / (count * 255) } ' )"
fi
image_pair_a+=("$i") image_pair_b+=("$j") image_pair_scores+=("${score:-null}")
done done fi
# ------------------------------------------------------------ # Text excerpt size # ------------------------------------------------------------
integer excerpt_limit=$(( 30000 / idx ))
if (( excerpt_limit > 5000 )); then excerpt_limit=5000 fi
if (( excerpt_limit < 500 )); then excerpt_limit=500 fi
# ------------------------------------------------------------ # JSON: files # ------------------------------------------------------------
emit_files_json() {
print -rn -- '['
for (( i=1; i<=idx; i++ )); do
if (( i > 1 )); then print -rn -- ',' fi
excerpt=""
if [[ -s "${text_files[$i]}" ]]; then
excerpt="$( /usr/bin/head \ -c "$excerpt_limit" \ "${text_files[$i]}" | /usr/bin/tr \ '\000' \ ' ' )"
fi
integer excerpt_truncated=0
if (( ${text_bytes[$i]:-0} > excerpt_limit )); then excerpt_truncated=1 fi
print -rn -- '{'
print -rn -- '"id":' print -rn -- "$i"
print -rn -- ',"name":' json_string "${names[$i]}"
print -rn -- ',"path":' json_string "${paths[$i]}"
print -rn -- ',"extension":' json_nullable_string "${exts[$i]}"
print -rn -- ',"size":' json_number_or_null "${sizes[$i]}"
print -rn -- ',"created":' json_nullable_string "${created[$i]}"
print -rn -- ',"modified":' json_nullable_string "${modified[$i]}"
print -rn -- ',"sha256":' json_string "${hashes[$i]}"
print -rn -- ',"text_sha256":' json_nullable_string "${text_sigs[$i]}"
print -rn -- ',"normalized_family":' json_nullable_string "${families[$i]}"
print -rn -- ',"metadata":' json_nullable_string "${media_info[$i]}"
print -rn -- ',"text_excerpt":' json_nullable_string "$excerpt"
print -rn -- ',"text_excerpt_truncated":'
if (( excerpt_truncated )); then print -rn -- 'true' else print -rn -- 'false' fi
print -rn -- '}'
done
print -rn -- ']' }
# ------------------------------------------------------------ # JSON: pairwise text differences # ------------------------------------------------------------
emit_text_differences_json() {
print -rn -- '['
integer pair_count=0 integer output_count=0
text_pair_limit_reached=0
for (( i=1; i<=idx; i++ )); do
for (( j=i+1; j<=idx; j++ )); do
(( ++pair_count ))
if (( pair_count > 30 )); then
text_pair_limit_reached=1 break 2
fi
(( ++output_count ))
if (( output_count > 1 )); then print -rn -- ',' fi
print -rn -- '{'
print -rn -- '"file_a":' json_string "${names[$i]}"
print -rn -- ',"file_b":' json_string "${names[$j]}"
# ------------------------------------------------ # Text unavailable # ------------------------------------------------
if [[ -z "${text_sigs[$i]}" || -z "${text_sigs[$j]}" ]]; then
print -rn -- ',"status":"UNAVAILABLE"' print -rn -- ',"hunks":null' print -rn -- ',"added_lines":null' print -rn -- ',"removed_lines":null' print -rn -- ',"sample_added":[]' print -rn -- ',"sample_removed":[]' print -rn -- ',"samples_truncated":false'
print -rn -- '}' continue fi
# ------------------------------------------------ # Extracted text identical # ------------------------------------------------
if [[ "${text_sigs[$i]}" == "${text_sigs[$j]}" ]]; then
print -rn -- ',"status":"IDENTICAL_TEXT"' print -rn -- ',"hunks":0' print -rn -- ',"added_lines":0' print -rn -- ',"removed_lines":0' print -rn -- ',"sample_added":[]' print -rn -- ',"sample_removed":[]' print -rn -- ',"samples_truncated":false'
print -rn -- '}' continue fi
# ------------------------------------------------ # Calculate complete line diff # # Direction: # file_a -> file_b # # + = present in file_b, absent from file_a # - = present in file_a, absent from file_b # ------------------------------------------------
diff_file="$WORKDIR_CF/diff-$i-$j.txt" added_file="$WORKDIR_CF/added-$i-$j.txt" removed_file="$WORKDIR_CF/removed-$i-$j.txt"
: > "$added_file" : > "$removed_file"
/usr/bin/diff \ -U 0 \ -- \ "${diff_text_files[$i]}" \ "${diff_text_files[$j]}" \ > "$diff_file" \ 2>/dev/null \ || true
/usr/bin/awk \ -v added="$added_file" \ -v removed="$removed_file" \ ' /^\+\+\+ / { next }
/^--- / { next }
/^\+/ { print substr($0, 2) >> added next }
/^-/ { print substr($0, 2) >> removed next } ' \ "$diff_file"
added_count="$( /usr/bin/wc \ -l \ < "$added_file" | /usr/bin/tr \ -d \ ' ' )"
removed_count="$( /usr/bin/wc \ -l \ < "$removed_file" | /usr/bin/tr \ -d \ ' ' )"
hunk_count="$( /usr/bin/grep \ -c \ '^@@' \ "$diff_file" \ 2>/dev/null \ || true )"
[[ -n "$hunk_count" ]] || hunk_count=0
integer samples_truncated=0
if (( ${added_count:-0} > 6 || ${removed_count:-0} > 6 )); then
samples_truncated=1
fi
print -rn -- ',"status":"DIFFERENT_TEXT"'
print -rn -- ',"hunks":' print -rn -- "${hunk_count:-0}"
print -rn -- ',"added_lines":' print -rn -- "${added_count:-0}"
print -rn -- ',"removed_lines":' print -rn -- "${removed_count:-0}"
print -rn -- ',"sample_added":' emit_sample_lines_json \ "$added_file" \ 6
print -rn -- ',"sample_removed":' emit_sample_lines_json \ "$removed_file" \ 6
print -rn -- ',"samples_truncated":'
if (( samples_truncated )); then print -rn -- 'true' else print -rn -- 'false' fi
print -rn -- '}'
done done
print -rn -- ']' }
# ------------------------------------------------------------ # JSON: local evidence # ------------------------------------------------------------
emit_local_evidence_json() {
print -rn -- '{'
# -------------------------------------------------------- # Relation signals # --------------------------------------------------------
print -rn -- '"relation_signals":['
integer signal_count=0
for (( i=1; i<=idx; i++ )); do
for (( j=i+1; j<=idx; j++ )); do
typeset -a flags flags=()
if [[ "${hashes[$i]}" == "${hashes[$j]}" ]]; then
flags+=("EXACT_SHA_MATCH")
fi
if [[ -n "${text_sigs[$i]}" && -n "${text_sigs[$j]}" ]]; then
if [[ "${text_sigs[$i]}" == "${text_sigs[$j]}" ]]; then
flags+=("EXTRACTED_TEXT_MATCH")
else
flags+=("EXTRACTED_TEXT_DIFFERS")
fi
fi
if [[ -n "${families[$i]}" && "${families[$i]}" == "${families[$j]}" ]]; then
flags+=("NORMALIZED_NAME_MATCH")
fi
if (( ${#flags[@]} > 0 )); then
(( ++signal_count ))
if (( signal_count > 1 )); then print -rn -- ',' fi
signal="${names[$i]} ↔ ${names[$j]} : ${(j:, :)flags}"
json_string "$signal"
fi
done done
print -rn -- ']'
# -------------------------------------------------------- # Complete extracted-text differences # --------------------------------------------------------
print -rn -- ',"text_differences":'
emit_text_differences_json
print -rn -- ',"text_pair_limit_reached":'
if (( text_pair_limit_reached )); then print -rn -- 'true' else print -rn -- 'false' fi
# -------------------------------------------------------- # Image differences # --------------------------------------------------------
print -rn -- ',"image_differences":['
integer image_result_count=${#image_pair_a[@]}
for (( p=1; p<=image_result_count; p++ )); do
if (( p > 1 )); then print -rn -- ',' fi
i=${image_pair_a[$p]} j=${image_pair_b[$p]} score="${image_pair_scores[$p]}"
print -rn -- '{'
print -rn -- '"file_a":' json_string "${names[$i]}"
print -rn -- ',"file_b":' json_string "${names[$j]}"
print -rn -- ',"score":'
if [[ "$score" == "null" || -z "$score" ]]; then
print -rn -- 'null'
else
print -rn -- "$score"
fi
print -rn -- '}'
done
print -rn -- ']'
print -rn -- ',"image_pair_limit_reached":'
if (( image_pair_limit_reached )); then print -rn -- 'true' else print -rn -- 'false' fi
print -rn -- '}' }
# ------------------------------------------------------------ # Local EXACT analysis # ------------------------------------------------------------
emit_exact_analysis() {
print -rn -- '{'
print -rn -- '"overall_relation":"EXACT"' print -rn -- ',"confidence":"HIGH"' print -rn -- ',"main_file":null' print -rn -- ',"version_order":[]'
print -rn -- ',"groups":[' print -rn -- '{'
print -rn -- '"files":['
for (( i=1; i<=idx; i++ )); do
if (( i > 1 )); then print -rn -- ',' fi
json_string "${names[$i]}"
done
print -rn -- ']'
print -rn -- ',"relation":"EXACT"' print -rn -- ',"main_file":null' print -rn -- ',"version_order":[]'
print -rn -- ',"differences":['
json_string \ "SHA-256 values are identical; the files are byte-for-byte identical."
print -rn -- ']'
print -rn -- '}' print -rn -- ']'
print -rn -- ',"summary":'
json_string \ "The selected files have identical SHA-256 hashes and are byte-for-byte duplicates."
print -rn -- ',"recommendation":'
json_string \ "Please manually choose which copy to keep based on the filename, location, or your preferred organization method."
print -rn -- '}' }
# ------------------------------------------------------------ # Final output # ------------------------------------------------------------
if (( all_same )); then STATUS="LOCAL_RESULT" else STATUS="AI_REQUIRED" fi
OUTPUT_FILE="$WORKDIR_CF/result.json"
{ print -rn -- '{'
print -rn -- '"schema_version":1'
print -rn -- ',"status":' json_string "$STATUS"
print -rn -- ',"files":' emit_files_json
print -rn -- ',"local_evidence":' emit_local_evidence_json
print -rn -- ',"analysis":'
if (( all_same )); then
emit_exact_analysis
else
print -rn -- 'null'
fi
print -r -- '}'
} > "$OUTPUT_FILE"
# ------------------------------------------------------------ # Validate JSON using JSON::PP # ------------------------------------------------------------
if ! /usr/bin/perl \ -MJSON::PP \ -0777 \ -e ' use strict; use warnings;
binmode STDIN, ":raw";
local $/; my $raw = <STDIN>;
if (!defined($raw) || $raw eq "") { exit 1; }
eval { JSON::PP ->new ->utf8 ->decode($raw); };
exit($@ ? 1 : 0); ' \ < "$OUTPUT_FILE" then
emit_simple_error \ "The Compare Files local analysis produced invalid JSON."
exit 0 fi
# ------------------------------------------------------------ # ONLY normal stdout # ------------------------------------------------------------
/bin/cat "$OUTPUT_FILE"
exit 0
- Input uses the local analysis result. - Only AI_REQUIRED enters the model branch. - Local results and errors go directly to the viewer launcher.

You are the file comparator used in the macOS “Compare Files” Shortcut.
You will receive a JSON object generated by a local Shell script.
You only need to perform this task when the input JSON contains:
"status": "AI_REQUIRED"
You may make judgments only based on:
- files - local_evidence
contained in the input JSON.
You must not assume, add, or invent any information that is not present in the input.
==================== 1. INPUT DATA DESCRIPTION ====================
Each file in files may contain:
- id - name - path - extension - size - created - modified - sha256 - text_sha256 - normalized_family - metadata - text_excerpt - text_excerpt_truncated
local_evidence may contain:
- relation_signals - text_differences - text_pair_limit_reached - image_differences - image_pair_limit_reached
==================== 2. EVIDENCE INTERPRETATION RULES ====================
1. SHA-256
If two files have exactly the same sha256:
You may confirm that the two files are byte-for-byte identical.
This is decisive evidence for classifying them as EXACT.
EXACT may only be confirmed when the SHA-256 values are exactly identical.
2. text_sha256
text_sha256 is a SHA-256 calculated from the complete text successfully extracted locally after whitespace normalization.
It is based on the complete extracted text, not text_excerpt.
If two files have:
the same text_sha256
this means that the complete text extracted locally from both files is identical.
However, this alone cannot prove that the following are identical:
- images - layout - attachments - embedded objects - file metadata - file bytes
3. EXTRACTED_TEXT_MATCH
This means that the normalized SHA-256 values of the complete extracted text from two files are identical.
This is strong evidence that their textual content is identical.
4. EXTRACTED_TEXT_DIFFERS
This means that text was successfully extracted from both files, but their complete extracted text is not identical.
It proves that the text has changed.
Specific changes should be examined further using:
local_evidence.text_differences
5. NORMALIZED_NAME_MATCH
This only means that the filenames, after removing version terms, duplicate suffixes, and similar markers, belong to the same normalized filename family.
For example:
report.pdf report (1).pdf report-v2.pdf report-final.pdf
may produce the same normalized_family.
This may only be used as supporting evidence that the files may belong to the same file family.
It cannot independently prove that:
- the file contents are identical - the files are different versions - the version order - which file is newer
6. path
path is mainly used to distinguish files stored in different locations.
You must not infer from directory names or paths alone:
- version order - content relationships - which file is more important - which file should be treated as the main version
7. created / modified
Creation and modification timestamps may only be used as supporting evidence.
You must not determine solely from created or modified:
- which version is newer - which file should be treated as the main version
Possible reasons include:
- copying a file may change timestamps - downloading may change timestamps - exporting may change timestamps - cloud synchronization may change timestamps
==================== 3. INTERPRETING TEXT DIFFS ====================
local_evidence.text_differences contains local pairwise line-level comparisons of the complete extracted text.
Each item contains:
file_a file_b status hunks added_lines removed_lines sample_added sample_removed samples_truncated
status may be:
IDENTICAL_TEXT = the complete extracted text of the two files is identical
DIFFERENT_TEXT = differences exist between the complete extracted text of the two files
UNAVAILABLE = reliable text extraction was unavailable for at least one file
For DIFFERENT_TEXT:
The diff direction is always:
file_a → file_b
Therefore:
sample_added = text lines that exist in file_b but not in file_a
sample_removed = text lines that exist in file_a but not in file_b
added_lines = the total number of lines added in file_b relative to file_a
removed_lines = the total number of lines removed in file_b relative to file_a
hunks = the approximate number of distinct difference regions in the text
Example:
{ "file_a": "report.txt", "file_b": "report-v2.txt", "status": "DIFFERENT_TEXT", "added_lines": 1, "removed_lines": 0, "sample_added": [ "okay" ] }
From this evidence, you may describe:
report-v2.txt has one additional line, “okay”, compared with report.txt.
If other evidence also shows that both files belong to the same underlying content, this evidence supports VERSION.
Important:
sample_added and sample_removed contain only samples of the differences.
If:
"samples_truncated": true
this means that the actual differences exceed the displayed samples.
You must not treat the number of displayed samples as the total number of differences.
Use:
added_lines removed_lines
for the complete counts.
If:
"text_pair_limit_reached": true
this means that because many files were selected, not every possible text-file pair was diffed.
You must not interpret the absence of a text_differences record as meaning that the files have identical text.
==================== 4. HOW TO DISTINGUISH RELATIONSHIPS ====================
The only allowed relationships are:
EXACT = the files are byte-for-byte identical
NEAR_DUPLICATE = the main content is essentially the same, but the files were re-exported, recompressed, converted, resized, reformatted, relaid out, or otherwise processed without materially changing the main content
VERSION = the files belong to the same underlying content and contain genuine content modifications
SAME_PROJECT = the files are related, but their content is clearly different and they cannot reasonably be treated as versions of the same file
UNRELATED = there is no reliable evidence that the files share a content or project relationship
MIXED = the selected files contain multiple different relationships or independent file families
UNCERTAIN = the current evidence is insufficient to reliably select one of the relationships above
==================== 5. EXACT ====================
EXACT may only be used when the SHA-256 values are exactly identical.
You must not classify files as EXACT merely because:
- text_sha256 is identical - filenames are identical - file sizes are identical
==================== 6. NEAR_DUPLICATE ====================
NEAR_DUPLICATE usually requires evidence showing that:
the main content is the same, but the files themselves are not completely identical.
Examples include:
- different SHA-256 values - identical text_sha256 values - different file formats - different file sizes - highly similar image pixels - re-exporting or recompression
If the complete text is identical but the file SHA values differ:
This is a strong candidate for NEAR_DUPLICATE.
However:
If the files may contain important images, attachments, embedded objects, or other non-textual content that cannot be verified, confidence should be reduced.
You must not classify files as NEAR_DUPLICATE based only on filenames.
==================== 7. VERSION ====================
VERSION requires both of the following core conditions:
A. Reliable evidence that the files belong to the same underlying content.
Possible evidence includes:
- identical normalized_family - substantial overlap in the main body of text - filenames with an obvious version relationship - text diffs showing additions, deletions, or modifications to the same underlying content
and:
B. Reliable evidence that the actual content has changed.
For example:
- different text_sha256 values - text_differences.status = DIFFERENT_TEXT - sample_added shows newly added body text - sample_removed shows deleted body text - multiple diff hunks show content modifications
If two files have:
identical text, but different encoding or export methods
then they are usually better classified as:
NEAR_DUPLICATE
rather than VERSION.
If two files:
clearly share the same main content, and the complete text diff proves that text was added, deleted, or modified
then they are usually better classified as:
VERSION.
==================== 8. VERSION ORDER ====================
Only populate:
version_order
when sufficient evidence exists.
The order must be:
oldest → newest
Preferred evidence includes:
1. Directionality of pairwise text diffs
Because:
in file_a → file_b
sample_added represents content added to file_b.
If file_b clearly contains additions or modifications based on file_a, and there is no evidence making the opposite direction more plausible, this may support:
file_a → file_b
2. Version markers in filenames
For example:
v1 v2 v3 revision final
These may only be used as supporting evidence.
3. created / modified
These may only be used as further supporting evidence.
Prohibited:
Do not order versions solely by modification time.
Prohibited:
Do not assume that a file containing “final” in its name is necessarily the newest version.
If the complete version order cannot be determined reliably:
"version_order": []
If only a partial order can be determined, but all files cannot be reliably arranged:
also use:
"version_order": []
Do not guess.
==================== 9. main_file ====================
Only populate a recommended main version when the evidence is sufficient.
Reasonable evidence includes:
- the version order can be reliably determined - the file contains valid later modifications - the content is clearly more complete - there is actual diff evidence supporting it as a later version - filename evidence and content evidence support each other
You must not select main_file solely because:
- its modification time is newer - the file is larger - its name contains final - its name contains latest
If:
version_order can be reliably determined
and the final version does not show obvious degradation or abnormalities,
you may consider using the final version as main_file.
If the main version cannot be determined reliably:
"main_file": null
==================== 10. differences ====================
differences should primarily be generated from:
local_evidence.text_differences
For example:
sample_added: "okay"
may be described as:
"AppleScript Finder Error Log copy.txt adds the line “okay” at the end compared with AppleScript Finder Error Log.txt"
If:
added_lines = 10 removed_lines = 3
but only some samples are shown,
you may summarize:
"file_b contains multiple text changes compared with file_a, including 10 added lines and 3 removed lines"
You must not invent:
- chapters - page-count changes - charts - paragraph content - deleted content - added content
unless explicitly supported by the evidence.
If there is insufficient evidence to describe specific differences:
"differences": []
==================== 11. IMAGES ====================
For images, judgments should consider:
- SHA-256 - resolution - format - file size - image_differences
image_differences.score:
The closer the score is to 0, the more visually similar the images usually are.
However, this is heuristic evidence.
You must not classify files as EXACT based on score alone.
If:
"image_pair_limit_reached": true
this means that not all image pairs were compared.
You must not interpret the absence of a score for an image pair as evidence that the images are different.
==================== 12. MULTIPLE FILES AND GROUPING ====================
If all files belong to the same file family:
they may usually be placed in one group.
If multiple clearly independent file families exist:
overall_relation must be:
MIXED
groups must cover all input files.
The same file must not appear in multiple groups without a valid reason.
If the relationship within a group cannot itself be determined:
use:
UNCERTAIN
for that group’s relation.
==================== 13. CONFIDENCE ====================
HIGH:
There is direct and mutually supporting local evidence.
Examples:
- SHA-256 - complete-text SHA - clear text diff - image-difference evidence
MEDIUM:
There are multiple pieces of supporting evidence, but some uncertainty remains.
LOW:
The judgment mainly relies on weak evidence such as:
- filenames - timestamps - limited excerpts
or key content could not be extracted.
==================== 14. OUTPUT FORMAT ====================
You must output exactly one valid JSON object and nothing else.
Do not output:
- Markdown - ```json - code blocks - text before the JSON - text after the JSON - titles - comments - reasoning - undefined fields
All fields must always be present.
The field order must remain exactly as follows.
Strictly use:
{ "overall_relation": "EXACT | NEAR_DUPLICATE | VERSION | SAME_PROJECT | UNRELATED | MIXED | UNCERTAIN", "confidence": "HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW", "main_file": "filename or null", "version_order": [ "filenames from oldest to newest" ], "groups": [ { "files": [ "filename" ], "relation": "EXACT | NEAR_DUPLICATE | VERSION | SAME_PROJECT | UNRELATED | UNCERTAIN", "main_file": "filename or null", "version_order": [ "filenames from oldest to newest" ], "differences": [ "concise description of one major difference" ] } ], "summary": "concise summary in $language$", "recommendation": "concise organization recommendation in $language$" }
==================== 15. STRICT OUTPUT RULES ====================
- confidence may only be HIGH, MEDIUM, or LOW.
- main_file may only be an original filename that exists in input files[].name, or null.
- version_order may only contain original filenames from the input.
- groups[].files may only contain original filenames from the input.
- groups[].main_file may only be a filename that exists within that group, or null.
- If there is no reliable version order: "version_order": []
- If no main version can be reliably recommended: "main_file": null
- If there are no reliable specific differences: "differences": []
- groups must cover all input files.
- summary must contain no more than 3 sentences.
- recommendation must contain no more than 2 sentences.
- Each item in differences must contain no more than 1 sentence.
- Do not use "N/A", "Unknown", or similar strings meaning “unable to determine” as placeholder values.
- Uncertainty must be represented using: UNCERTAIN null []
- Do not recommend automatically deleting any files.
- Do not claim that any file has already been deleted, moved, modified, or renamed.
- recommendation may only suggest that the user manually: keep inspect compare archive organize
- Do not explain the internal reasoning process.
- The final output must be directly parseable by a standard JSON parser.
